title: .NET reading: background decompression
dataset: 1,000,000 rows × 10 columns, written by the Hypaxel writer with inline or shared strings, read cell by cell
method: From the .NET 10 --read-quick run: the best of three runs and the CPU time of that run, summed over all threads.
notes: With several readers at once on the 10 cores (inline file, one process per reader, each reporting its best of three), a read takes 0.76–0.77 s by default and 0.53–0.54 s with it for 4 readers, but 0.84–0.89 s and 0.92–1.05 s for 10 readers.

It saves about 30% of the time when cores are idle but costs 15 to 20% more CPU; when every core is busy it makes the total slower, which is why it is off by default. Each open worksheet holds 1 MiB of buffers (four 256 KiB chunks) while it is on.
reproduce:
cd dotnet/benchmarks/Hypaxel.Benchmarks
dotnet run -c Release -f net10.0 -- --read-quick 1000000                    # all readers, both files
dotnet run -c Release -f net10.0 -- --read-quick 1000000 Sylvan shared      # one reader, one file
